title: More US Households Now Have Kittens than Puppies
paragraphs: Cats don't need much space, they don't usually mind being left alone, and they won't complain if you spend Saturday on the sofa.
And new data shows that, for the first time, more US households are choosing kittens over puppies.

According to market research company Packaged Facts, in 2014 there were 1.8 US households with a dog under 1 year old for every household with a cat of the same age. By 2025, the numbers were equal. And in 2026, there were 0.94 puppy-owning households for every household with a kitten.
However, dogs are still America's most popular pet. According to the American Pet Products Association, 71 million US households owned a dog in 2025, while 53 million had a cat.
But when it comes to getting new pets, why are fewer Americans choosing puppies?
Dogs often need more care, and they can cost more too. Packaged Facts says that owners spend about $1,300 a year on a dog, but only around $750 on a cat.

Housing could also be affecting people's decisions. According to Packaged Facts, homeowners are almost twice as likely as renters to own a dog. With home prices going up and more people living in small apartments, cats may be a better fit for modern life.
And cat lovers recently got another piece of good news. A September study done across 93 countries found that those with more cats per person tended to report higher levels of happiness.
So dogs may still be America's favorite pet, but cats seem to be having a very good year!
